objects.description: Simple 2D point with double-precision coordinates and a stream insertion operator.
A 128-bit UUID union with multiple integer views and helpers to generate random UUID-like values and to format as dashed hex string. Comparison operators compare the 128-bit value lexicographically.

functions.name: util::fail_guard
functions.description: Constructs a scope guard that calls the provided callable f when the guard is destroyed, but only if the guard's failure flag remains true. Use to ensure rollback/cleanup on failure paths. Call disable() on the returned guard to prevent invocation on destruction.
requirements: f must be an invocable object callable with no arguments and noexcept-safety is recommended because it is called in a destructor.
The callable must remain valid inside the guard (it is moved into the guard).
Destruction order: cleanup is executed during the guard’s destructor if failure is true.

functions.name: util::append_struct
functions.signature: template<class T> void append_struct(std::vector<uint8_t> &buf, const T &value)
functions.description: Appends a byte-wise copy of value to the end of buf. Useful for serializing POD-like structures into a byte buffer.
requirements: buf is a valid std::vector<uint8_t> and is modifiable.
T is treated as a sequence of sizeof(T) bytes; callers should only use trivially copyable/standard-layout types to avoid UB related to object representation and padding.
The lifetime of value must extend through the call.

functions.name: util::hex
functions.signature: template<class T> util::Hex<T> hex(const T &elem, bool rev = false)
functions.description: Returns a utility wrapper that formats elem’s raw bytes as an uppercase hexadecimal string. If rev is true, bytes are emitted from lowest to highest address; otherwise from highest to lowest.
requirements: T is read as raw bytes; use trivially copyable types for portability.
Endianness and sizeof(T) affect the textual result.
The returned Hex<T> must be converted to string or string_view before use as text.

functions.name: util::log_hex
functions.description: Formats value as a hexadecimal string prefixed with "0x" using util::Hex with non-reversed byte order.
requirements: T is read as raw bytes; use trivially copyable types for portability.
Endianness and sizeof(T) affect the output.

functions.name: util::hex_vec
functions.signature: template<class It> std::string hex_vec(It begin, It end, bool rev = false)
functions.description: Converts a range of elements to a contiguous uppercase hex string by interpreting each element’s value as a byte. If rev is false, emits bytes in reverse iterator order; if true, in forward order.
requirements: It must be a random-access iterator or pointer supporting end - begin.
Value type must be convertible to uint8_t (e.g., unsigned char, std::byte, or integral).
The range [begin, end) must be valid.
rev selects forward (true) vs reverse (false) emission order.

functions.name: util::from_hex
functions.signature: template<class T> T from_hex(const std::string_view &hex, bool rev = false)
functions.description: Parses hex-encoded characters from hex into a value of type T by filling sizeof(T) bytes. Non-hex characters are ignored. If rev is true, the resulting byte buffer is reversed before reinterpretation as T.
requirements: T must be trivially copyable with no trap representations; the function constructs T from raw bytes via reinterpret_cast.
hex may contain arbitrary characters; only 0-9, a-f, A-F are parsed. Two hex digits make one byte; odd trailing nibble is paired with next valid nibble encountered from the end.
If fewer than sizeof(T) bytes are present, the high-order portion is zero-padded.
The returned value’s interpretation is endianness- and layout-dependent.

functions.name: util::from_hex_vec
functions.signature: inline std::string from_hex_vec(const std::string &hex, bool rev = false)
functions.description: Parses hex-encoded characters in hex into a byte string (std::string of bytes). Non-hex characters are ignored. If rev is true, reverses the resulting byte sequence.
requirements: hex may contain arbitrary characters; only 0-9, a-f, A-F are parsed.
Two hex digits form one output byte; ignores non-hex between digits.
Output size is floor(count(hex-digits)/2).

functions.name: util::enm
functions.signature: template<class T> auto enm(const T &val) -> const std::underlying_type_t<T> &
functions.description: Returns a reference to the underlying integer representation of an enum value (const overload). Enables treating enum as its underlying type without a cast.
requirements: T must be an enumeration type (std::is_enum_v<T>).
The reference is produced via reinterpret_cast; only use with standard C++ enums where object representation matches the underlying type.
The lifetime of val must outlive any use of the returned reference.

functions.name: util::from_chars
functions.signature: inline std::int64_t from_chars(const char *begin, const char *end)
functions.description: Parses a decimal integer from the character range [begin, end). Supports an optional leading '-' and digits '0'..'9'. Returns 0 if the range is empty.
requirements: begin and end must denote a valid contiguous character range; end can equal begin.
Only ASCII digits are expected; behavior is not validated for other characters (non-digits will produce unspecified results).
No overflow checking is performed; callers must ensure the value fits in int64_t.

functions.name: util::from_view
functions.description: Parses a decimal integer from number by delegating to util::from_chars.
requirements: number should contain an optional leading '-' followed by ASCII digits; no overflow checking is performed.
Returns 0 for an empty string.

functions.name: util::either
functions.description: Returns l.value() if l has a value, otherwise returns r. The result is returned by value; l is moved-from when engaged and r is perfectly forwarded otherwise.
requirements: T must be movable/copyable since the result is returned by value.
If l has a value, that value is moved; r is not evaluated by this function (it is an argument).

functions.name: util::c_free
functions.description: Calls free(p). Utility suited for custom deleters for C-allocated memory.
requirements: p must be a pointer obtained from a compatible C allocation function (malloc/calloc/realloc) or null.
Do not pass pointers to C++-allocated objects (new/delete) or non-heap pointers.

functions.name: util::dynamic
functions.signature: template<class T, class ReturnType, ReturnType (**function)(T *)> void dynamic(T *p)
functions.description: Invokes an indirect function pointer stored at address function with argument p. Intended as a generic deleter wrapper for APIs exposing function pointers that may be set at runtime.
requirements: function must point to a valid function pointer variable of type ReturnType (*)(T*).
The pointed-to function must be callable for the provided p. Any return value is ignored by this wrapper.
Thread-safety and initialization of the function pointer are the caller’s responsibility.

functions.name: util::view
functions.signature: template<class It> std::string_view view(It begin, It end)
functions.description: Creates a std::string_view over the raw bytes in the half-open range [begin, end). begin and end are interpreted as pointers/iterators to byte-sized elements and are reinterpreted as const char*.
requirements: It must be a random-access iterator or pointer where end - begin yields the byte count.
The underlying memory must be contiguous and remain valid for the lifetime of the returned string_view.
Elements must be byte-addressable and convertible to const char (e.g., uint8_t*, char*, std::byte*).

functions.name: util::endian::little
functions.signature: template<class T> inline T little(T x)
functions.description: Converts x to little-endian byte order by reversing its bytes on big-endian targets; returns x unchanged on little-endian targets. Supports std::optional<T> by conditionally swapping contained value.
requirements: T must be treated as a sequence of bytes; prefer trivially copyable types.
For optional types, only std::optional<U> is supported; empty optionals remain empty.
Behavior depends on target endianness at compile time.

functions.name: util::endian::big
functions.signature: template<class T> inline T big(T x)
functions.description: Converts x to big-endian byte order by reversing its bytes on little-endian targets; returns x unchanged on big-endian targets. Supports std::optional<T> by conditionally swapping contained value.
requirements: T must be treated as a sequence of bytes; prefer trivially copyable types.
For optional types, only std::optional<U> is supported; empty optionals remain empty.
Behavior depends on target endianness at compile time.

functions.name: uuid_util::uuid_t::generate
functions.description: Generates a 128-bit UUID-like value using the provided engine to fill 16 bytes uniformly, then masks specific bits for variant/version compatibility. Returns the resulting uuid_t.
requirements: engine must be a valid, initialized std::default_random_engine.
Resulting UUID bytes are derived from uniform uint8_t distribution; no I/O or exceptions are expected.

functions.name: uuid_util::uuid_t::generate
functions.description: Generates a 128-bit UUID-like value using std::random_device to seed a std::default_random_engine, then delegates to the engine-based overload.
requirements: System must permit constructing std::random_device; quality of randomness depends on platform.
No parameters; returns a freshly generated uuid_t.

functions.name: uuid_util::uuid_t::string
functions.description: Returns the canonical hyphenated hexadecimal representation of the UUID (8-4-4-4-12 groups, uppercase hex). The formatting uses util::hex with byte-order suitable for UUID text.
requirements: The uuid_t object must be valid.
The returned string is newly allocated and independent of the source object.

data_types.description: A buffer of uninterpreted bytes. Any byte values 0x00–0xFF in any order and length. Often sourced from FUZZ_PARAM_STR and treated as raw binary without encoding assumptions.

A text containing hexadecimal digits representing bytes. May include non-hex characters which should be ignored by tolerant parsers. Valid hex digits are 0-9, a-f, A-F; every two hex digits map to one byte. Length may be odd and may be mixed with separators or junk.

An ASCII string representing a signed decimal integer: optionally a single leading '-' followed by digits 0-9. May be empty; some parsers might also encounter stray non-digit characters but expect only digits and optional leading minus.

generators.generator:
import random
from typing import List

# Target data type: decimal integer string
# Fuzzer stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_STR to get an initial string, then rewrite its
# characters into digit-heavy content with possible leading '-'. Our goal is to
# supply initial buffers that, after the stubâ€™s transformation, still produce
# interesting valid inputs across size/shape boundaries.
#
# Strategy:
# - Generate a variety of numeric-like strings:
#   - empty string
#   - single digit
#   - long sequences (up to 64 per stub cap)
#   - with/without leading '-'
#   - boundary lengths: 1, 2, 18, 19, 20, 63, 64
#   - sequences of all same digit, alternating digits, random digits
# - Because the stub overwrites many characters, we bias our bytes to ASCII
#   digits and '-' so the post-rewrite stays within expectations.
# - We also include occasional non-digit 'x' since one stub may set some chars
#   to 'x'. Parsers ignore non-digits in from_chars according to description,
#   but we focus on valid numeric strings primarily.
#
# The function returns bytes; FUZZ_PARAM_STR will interpret these as a string.

_DIGITS = "0123456789"


def _rand_digits(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    return "".join(rng.choice(_DIGITS) for _ in range(max(0, n)))


def _alternating_digits(n: int) -> str:
    if n <= 0:
        return ""
    return ("10" * (n // 2)) + ("1" if n % 2 else "")


def _repeat_digit(d: str, n: int) -> str:
    return d * max(0, n)


def _with_optional_minus(rng: random.Random, s: str, force: bool | None = None) -> str:
    if not s:
        return s
    place_minus = force if force is not None else rng.choice([True, False])
    return ("-" + s) if place_minus else s


def _make_candidate_set(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    # Core lengths influenced by stub caps and typical integer limits
    lens = [0, 1, 2, 18, 19, 20, 63, 64]
    candidates: List[str] = []

    # Empty
    candidates.append("")

    # Single-digit and small numbers
    for d in ["0", "1", "9"]:
        candidates.append(d)
    candidates.append("-0")

    # Boundary-sized digit strings
    for L in lens:
        if L == 0:
            continue
        # pure random digits
        s = _rand_digits(rng, L)
        candidates.append(_with_optional_minus(rng, s))

        # repeating digit
        d = rng.choice(_DIGITS)
        s2 = _repeat_digit(d, L)
        candidates.append(_with_optional_minus(rng, s2))

        # alternating 1/0
        s3 = _alternating_digits(L)
        candidates.append(_with_optional_minus(rng, s3))

    # Strings starting with minus and maximum length 64 digits
    candidates.append("-" + _repeat_digit("9", 64))
    candidates.append("-" + _alternating_digits(64))

    # Mixed patterns under cap
    for _ in range(6):
        L = rng.randint(1, 64)
        # mix digits with occasional 'x'
        s = []
        for i in range(L):
            if rng.random() < 0.05:
                s.append('x')
            else:
                s.append(rng.choice(_DIGITS))
        mix = ''.join(s)
        candidates.append(_with_optional_minus(rng, mix))

    # Ensure variety of leading characters
    candidates.extend([
        "-" + _rand_digits(rng, 10),
        "0" + _rand_digits(rng, 10),
        "9" + _rand_digits(rng, 10),
    ])

    # Deduplicate while preserving order
    seen = set()
    uniq: List[str] = []
    for s in candidates:
        if s not in seen:
            seen.add(s)
            uniq.append(s)
    # Respect 4096 limit (well under)
    return uniq[:64]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a pool of candidate strings
    candidates = _make_candidate_set(rng)

    # Choose one according to seed and a little extra randomness
    idx = rng.randrange(len(candidates))
    s = candidates[idx]

    # Return as bytes (ASCII)
    return s.encode('ascii', errors='strict')
